blocks.text: This Name is mentioned once in the Noble Qur'aan combined with the Name Al-'Azeez The Almighty in Allaah's saying,

He is Allah than Whom there is La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He) the King, the Holy, the One Free from all defects, the Giver of security, the Watcher over His creatures, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glory be to Allah! (High is He) above all that they associate as partners with Him.

1. It has the meaning of Al-Qahhaar The Invincible Subduer. Allaah is the Subduer of everything. Everything submits to Him, everything humbles themselves to Him. The upper and lower world with all that is in it of amazing creation humbly submits their movements and their staying still and what comes and goes to their Owner and Controller. They do not have any control nor any rule over anything, instead the command is all for Allaah – the legislated, predestined and rule of recompense is all for Allaah. There is no judge except for Him, no Lord other than Him and no deity worthy of worship besides Him.

2. Al-Jabbaar refers to subtle kindness, mercy and compassion. Allaah is the One who heals the defeated, enriches the poor, makes things easy for the one in hardship and grants success to the sick and afflicted to have patience. He makes it easy for them and replaces their hardship for the greatest reward. He grants special compassion to the hearts of those who humble themselves to His greatness and honour and to those hearts who love Him. They humble themselves to His Perfection, hoping for His grace and favours out of what He has bestowed upon their hearts of love, different types of recognition, divine success, guidance and direction. A person making du'aa saying 'Allaahummajburnee' is asking for this 'jabr' compassion which in reality is the rectification of the servant, repelling all types of disliked matters and evils from him.
The Prophet ﷺ used to say between the two prostrations (sajdah) in salaah:
'O Allah! Pardon me, have mercy on me, help me, guide me, and grant me sustenance.'
blocks.ref: Jaami' at-Tirmidhee 284 and Sunan Ibn Maajah 898

blocks.text: 3. From the meanings of Al-Jabbaar is Al-'Alee The High and Exalted over everything. The One who encompasses all meanings of highness: highness of Himself, highness of status and highness of invincibility.

Power and Might (Al-Jabaroot) is for Allaah alone. Whoever from the creation brings about Allaah's anger, deserves His threat. Allaah has warned those who do this of a severe punishment, He will seal his heart and enter him into Hell Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Allaah said,
Thus does Allah seal up the heart of every arrogant, tyrant.
Ahmad and Tirmidhee related from Aboo Hurayrah who said that the Prophet ﷺ said,

"Some of the Fire (in the shape of a long neck) will come out of the Fire on the Day of Judgment. It will have two eyes which can see, two ears which can hear, and a tongue which can speak. It will say: 'I have been left in charge of three: Every obstinate oppressor, everyone who called upon a deity besides Allah, and the image makers.'"

keyPoints: Al-Jabbaar is mentioned once in the Qur'aan, combined with Al-'Azeez, in Hashr 59:23.
First meaning: Al-Qahhaar, the Invincible Subduer to whom everything submits and humbles itself.
Second meaning: subtle kindness, mercy and compassion – He heals the defeated, enriches the poor and eases hardship; saying 'Allaahummajburnee' asks for this jabr.
Third meaning: Al-'Alee, the High and Exalted over everything – in Himself, in status and in invincibility.
Power and Might (Al-Jabaroot) is for Allaah alone; the arrogant tyrant among the creation is threatened with a sealed heart and the Fire.

recall.q: What are the three meanings of Al-Jabbaar?
recall.a: 1) Al-Qahhaar, the Invincible Subduer; 2) subtle kindness, mercy and compassion; 3) Al-'Alee, the High and Exalted over everything.

recall.q: Where is the Name Al-Jabbaar mentioned in the Qur'aan?
recall.a: Once, combined with Al-'Azeez, in Hashr 59:23.

recall.q: What is a person asking for when saying 'Allaahummajburnee'?
recall.a: The 'jabr' compassion, which in reality is the rectification of the servant and repelling all disliked matters and evils from him.

recall.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say between the two prostrations?
recall.a: 'O Allah! Pardon me, have mercy on me, help me, guide me, and grant me sustenance.'

recall.q: Which three will the neck of Fire say it has been left in charge of?
recall.a: Every obstinate oppressor, everyone who called upon a deity besides Allah, and the image makers.
